section_summary.extract_value: This section reports gender-specific hierarchical regression analyses predicting general sexual liberalism. For women (N inferred = 151), sexual orientation was a significant predictor in step 1, and in step 2 body appreciation, sexual orientation, and BMI were significant predictors. For men (Ns inferred = 163 and 161 across steps), only body appreciation emerged as a significant predictor in the second step; no explicit study numbering is given.
section_summary.evidence_source: Quoted sentences from the section: 'When general sexual liberalism was entered as the criterion variable, the first step of the regression was significant in women, F(4, 146) = 3.17, p = .016, Adj. R^2 = .06, with sexual orientation being the only significant predictor (B = .27, SE = .10, \beta = .22, t = 2.68, p = .008).' and 'The second step of the regression was also significant, F(8, 142) = 5.25, p < .001, \Delta R^2 = .13, with body appreciation (B = .35, SE = .15, \beta = .29, t = 2.39, p = .018), sexual orientation (B = .27, SE = .09, \beta = .22, t = 2.90, p = .004), and BMI (B = .03, SE = .01, \beta = .20, t = 2.41, p = .017) emerging as significant predictors.' and 'In men, the first step of the regression did not reach significance, F(4, 158) < 1, Adj. R^2 < .01, whereas the second step did, F(8, 152) = 3.21, p = .001, \Delta R^2 = .10. Of the variables entered into the second step, the only significant predictor was body appreciation (B = .25, SE = .11, \beta = .24, t = 2.25, p = .026).'
